Frequently asked questions

Short answers to common questions. For step-by-step instructions, see the guide.

Is Vocal Harmony Maker free?
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no account.
Is my song uploaded?
No. The song is read, separated, analyzed, and played only in your browser. Nothing about it is sent anywhere. See the privacy policy.
What does it make?
From the song you choose, four parts with their own faders: the vocals and the backing (separated with AI), and a harmony part as two parts — the singer's voice moved to the harmony notes, and a plain guide tone on the same notes. It also shows the tempo (BPM), a chord on every beat, the melody, and the harmony notes.
Which harmony parts can it make?
A 3rd above (the most common), a 3rd below, a 5th above, or a 5th below the melody. The notes are chosen in the key of the song and moved to a chord tone where they would clash, so a “3rd” is sometimes a 4th. See upper or lower, 3rd or 5th.
Can it make two harmonies at once (three-part harmony)?
One at a time. To get two, make one part (for example a 3rd above) and save “Harmony (voice)” as MP3, then choose another part (a 3rd below), remake the harmony, and save it too. Layer the files in a recording app.
Which files can I open?
Any audio format your browser can play: MP3, WAV, M4A (AAC), FLAC, Ogg, and others, and videos such as MP4, MOV, and WebM (the app uses their sound). Songs up to 12 minutes (8 minutes on phones and tablets).
Can I use songs from Apple Music, Spotify, or YouTube?
No. Music from streaming services is protected and cannot be opened in other apps. Use audio files you have, such as your own recordings or songs you bought as files.
Can I use a recording of my own singing?
Yes, and it works well: with a voice alone (or a voice and a guitar), separation is easy, and the harmony is made from your own voice. A steady tempo and clear chords help the chords come out right.
How long does it take?
On a recent computer, usually less than the length of the song; faster with a browser that supports WebGPU. Phones and tablets take longer. The harmony then takes a few more seconds.
Why is there a large download?
The AI model (about 75 MB) runs on your device, so the browser has to download it once. It is kept, so the next time there is no download. On mobile data the app asks first. ⚙ → “Delete the AI model” frees the space.
The page reloaded, or separation stopped partway.
The device ran out of memory. Close other tabs and apps and try again: the app uses a lighter setting next time. If it keeps stopping, try a shorter song or use a computer.
The harmony voice sounds strange in places.
It is the separated vocals moved to other notes, so anything that stayed in the vocals (a guitar doubling the melody, backing vocals, reverb) moves too, and large moves make a voice sound a little different. The guide tone has exact, clean notes. See why it is not perfect.
A harmony note sounds wrong.
Usually the chord at that beat was estimated wrong. Tap the beat in the chord row, type the right chord, and press “Remake the harmony”. See editing the chords.
Is it the harmony of the original record?
No. The app writes its own harmony from the melody, the key, and the chords. If the record has a harmony part, learn that one by ear; the app's harmony is a starting point and a practice tool.
Can I change the key?
Yes, up to 12 semitones up or down, without changing the tempo. The vocals, the backing, the chord names, and the harmony all follow. See changing the key.
Is the harmony saved?
Not in the app: the parts, the chords, and the harmony are gone when you reload or choose another song. Save the ones you want as MP3 files (192 kbps) with the ↓ buttons or “Save this mix (MP3)”. The mixer settings (faders, mute, master volume) are remembered.
Which songs can I use, and can I publish what I made?
Use your own recordings, or songs whose rights you have. For your own practice at home, using a song you bought is usually fine; publishing or sharing a separated or harmonized version of someone else's song usually needs the permission of the rights holders.
Can I use it offline?
After your first separation, the app, the AI model, and the separation engine are kept on your device, so it opens and works without a connection. You can also add it to your home screen.
